newsitem.title: UK: Landround plans July AIM float and enhanced status.
newsitem.headline: Landround plans July AIM float and enhanced status.

text.p: Landround Plc said on Tuesday it was planning a July flotation on the London Stock Exchange's Alternative Investment Market (AIM), with the principal aim of raising its profile among blue chip clients.
Landround, which supplies leisure break promotions to companies, said the AIM float would increase the credibility of the company and allay any fears potential customers might have with its products.
"Many companies coming to AIM say they want the increased profile the float provides and we are certainly not paying lip service to this," said chairman and chief executive Michael Crompton.
"We need the status the quote will give. It will enhance our marketing ability."
Landround, based in Chester, sells travel promotions supplied by groups such as of P&O, Cunard and British Airways Holidays to companies which include BT, Coca Cola and Dixons.
The company said it hoped to raise between one and 1.25 million stg - of which half a million would be new money - and the market capitalisation is expected to be about five million stg.
Dealings in the shares are expected to begin on July 7.
The company highlighted the cash generative nature of the business and said it had around 500,000 stg of cash in the bank.
"We don't need rocket scientists to run this business," said Crompton. "We just sell vouchers and put the profits in the bank."
Landround made pre-tax profits for the year-ended September 30 1996 of 362,000 stg against 239,000 stg for the previous year. Turnover was 2.31 million stg in 1996, up on 1.67 million stg in 1995.
Henry Ansbacher & Co and W H Ireland LTd have been appointed nominated adviser and broker respectively.
